subject: OCC1
title: Introduction to Professional Practice 1
description: Introduction to Occupational Therapy through interactive seminars.

subject: OCC1
title: Constructing Mental Health
description: This course provides foundational knowledge for occupational therapy practice in psychiatry from a historical and critical perspective. Students will have the opportunity to develop mental health literacy, and apply previously learned concepts for occupation-focused reasoning in the domain of mental illness and mental health.

restrictions.text: This course is only open to U2 students in the BSc. (Rehab.Sc); Major in Occupational Therapy.

subject: OCC1
title: Enabling Leisure Occupations
description: An examination of the concepts of leisure and play as occupations throughout the lifespan. Students will explore a variety of adapted leisure activities including those available within local community organizations and will appreciate the role of occupational therapy in, and importance of, enabling leisure occupations.

restrictions.text: This course is only open to students in the BSc. (Rehab.Sc); Major in Occupational Therapy.

subject: OCC1
title: Pre-Clinical Practicum Seminar
description: This compulsory seminar course will comprise 5 pre-clinical seminars of two hours each to be offered in the U3/QY year during the Fall term (one seminar; total of 2 hrs) and during the Winter term (4 seminars; total of 8 hrs). This course is a prerequisite for Clinical Practicum 1 and 2 (OCC1 501 and OCC1 502).

restrictions.text: Open only to students registered in the following programs: BSc Rehabilitation Science (Major Occupational Therapy) and MSc Applied Qualifying Year for Occupational Therapy.

notes: Students must register for both OCC1 500D1 and OCC1 500D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both OCC1 500D1 and OCC1 500D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: OCC1
title: Clinical Practicum 1
description: First supervised clinical practicum. Introduction to history taking, clinical reasoning, assessment and treatment for physical and psychiatric conditions.
notes: **Due to the COVID-19 situation, add/drop is the tenth lecture day and withdrawal is the thirteenth lecture day.

subject: OCC1
title: Clinical Practicum 2
description: Second supervised clinical practicum.
notes: **Due to the COVID-19 situation, add/drop is the eleventh lecture day and withdrawal is the fifteenth lecture day.

subject: OCC1
title: Clinical Practicum 3
description: Third supervised clinical practicum.

prerequisites.text: OCC1 502 and Fall Courses in M1 OT

subject: OCC1
title: Therapeutic Strategies in OT 1
description: Evaluation, intervention and planning using a neuromuscular skeletal framework.

subject: OCC1
title: Occupational Solutions 1
description: Assessment and treatment of clients with disorders of the nervous system.

subject: OCC1
title: Holistic Approaches in OT
description: The theory, principles of treatment, clinical reasoning and therapeutic use of activities in the OT intervention of acute and chronic medical and surgical conditions.

subject: OCC1
title: Therapeutic Strategies in OT 2
description: Advanced Therapeutic Strategies for systemic and complex conditions.

subject: OCC1
title: Enabling Human Occupation
description: Occupational performance (productivity, self-care, leisure) is examined through the Canadian Occupational Performance Model and the Model of Human Occupation, both of which focus on the interaction of the individual with the environment. Human performance is analyzed focusing on prevention of disability and/or restoration of function.

subject: OCC1
title: Psychosocial Practice in OT
description: Principles of basic psychosocial assessments and treatment approaches for psychiatric conditions.

subject: OCC1
title: Clinical Practicum Seminars
description: This compulsory course will comprise 9 pre-clinical seminars to be offered in the M1 and M2 years prior to Clinical Practicum 3 and 4. The seminars will be implemented during the M1 Summer term (1 seminar; total of 2 hrs), M1 Fall term (2 seminars; total of 4 hrs), M1 Winter term (5 seminars; total of 11.5 hrs) and the M2 Fall term (1 seminars; total of 1 hr). This course is a prerequisite for Clinical Practicum 3 and 4 (OCC1 503 and OCC1 602).

restrictions.text: Open only to students registered in the following program: M.Sc.(Applied) in Occupational Therapy.

notes: No credit will be given for this course unless OCC1 600J1, OCC1 600J2 and OCC1 600J3 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.
Students must register for OCC1 600J1, OCC1 600J2 and OCC1 600J3.

subject: OCC1
title: Clinical Practicum 4
description: Fourth clinical practicum.

subject: OCC1
title: Occupational Solutions 2
description: OT assessment and treatment of clients with disorders of the nervous system.

subject: OCC1
title: Applied OT: Psychosocial Theory
description: Current theories of psychosocial OT, including advanced psychosocial assessments and individual and/or group interventions relevant to specific psychosocial theories.

subject: OCC1
title: Work/Ergonomics
description: The principles of vocational rehabilitation including job demands analysis, functional capacity evaluation, and return to work. Examines environmental influences, ergonomic principles and assessment, the fitting of the workplace to the capabilities of the human worker, promotion of work safety, and injury prevention.

subject: OCC1
title: Community-Based OT
description: Assessment of community needs, development of OT community services, and the different roles of the OT in mental health and in the international community. Reintegration of the client in the socio-cultural community.

subject: OCC1
title: Assistive Technology
description: Application of high and low-technology assistive devices to enhance performance and individual human needs, including alternative computer access, manual and powered mobility, augmentative communication, telecommunications and environmental control, social and professional issues regarding technology service delivery.

subject: OCC1
title: Functional Environments
description: Problems and solutions of the environment that impact negatively on the physically or mentally disabled individual.

restrictions.text: M1 OT and Architecture students only

subject: OCC1
title: Mental Health: Child and Youth
description: Orientation to children and adolescents with psychiatric disorders as well as evaluation and remediation techniques.
